notes: Explosive remnants of war: On 31 March 2024, at least nine children including 5 girls and 4 boys were killed and five were wounded when a mine, remnants of war, exploded in the Zadran village of Giro district [coded to Pana], Ghazni. A Taliban spokesman said the bomb was from the war with the Soviet Union. Sources reported conflicting details regarding the nature of the death as some sources claimed the children were playing with the bomb when it exploded while others said a vehicle they were riding was hit with the bomb, and no details were provided about adult casualties.; On 21 March 2024, 21-43 Taliban members and civilians were killed and 50 were wounded when an IS suicide bomber detonated himself outside a bank in Shahidan Chawk area in PD1 of Kandahar city. The Taliban members were gathered to withdraw their salaries. The Taliban claimed 3 killed and 12 injured. Total fatalities coded as 22 to include the bomber.; On 18 March 2024, six civilians, three women and three children, were killed by Pakistan military airstrikes in the Laman area of Barmal district, Paktika. Pakistan military said they targeted TTP militants, but the group and the Taliban said civilians were killed in the attacks.; On 14 March 2024, five Taliban members were killed and two were wounded following an attack by National Resistance Front militants on a Taliban checkpoint near Serena Hotel, Kabul city. The hotel, which had local and foreign guests, is around 50 meters away from the Citadel. The sound of an explosion was reported in the area of the attack. Later on the same day, Taliban members in videos claimed they stopped 4 NRF members planning to conduct more attacks, and killed them, sharing images of bodies on media.

Police forces clashed with the gangsters in the vicinity and within the prison, resulting in at least 30 fatalities among police officers, penitentiary staff members, and prisoners. The corpses of the deceased were found around the prison and scattered in several nearby areas of the downtown. Some had gunshot wounds, some other were mutilated, burned, or tied up. An unknown number of prison workers and inmates were injured. Thousands of prisoners fled. Some imprisoned gangsters were released by their accomplices, while other inmates took the opportunity to escape. Around 90 prisoners decided to stay inside the prison when police forces left the building. They were described as the convicted in relation to the killing of President Jovenel Moise (coded separately). The gang members had spied on the facilities with a drone since 29 February. The prison's assault was part of coordinated attacks against the two major Haiti prisons led by the G-9 Gang with the support of gangs aligned to the Living Together Movement gang-led initiative (coded separately). Still that day, the Ministry of Culture and Communications (Bois Verna neighbourhood) was occupied and looted. Gunshots were heard in Champs de Mars, Lalue, Bas Delmas and Poste Marchand. notes: On 23 February 2024, 5 NPA militants and a police officer were killed in a joint operation of the 47th Infantry Battalion, 21st Special Forces Company, and Provincial Mobile Force Company in Barangay Campagao (Bilar, Bohol, Central Visayas). Authorities recovered weapons from the rebels.The Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP), National Union of Peoples' Lawyers (NUPL) Cebu, and human rights groups Karapatan said there was no armed encounter, and the 5 militants were apprehended alive and tortured by state forces. They said the militants were summarily executed, even though they were hors de combat and rendered unable to fight. NUPL Cebu said these killings are violations of International Humanitarian Law (IHL). Karapatan said the male militants were ordered to remove their shirts, and they were all ordered to roll in the mud to simulate a firefight with NPA members. The militant lawyer's cadaver showed signs stab wounds and bruises, indicating that they may have been tortured before they were summarily executed. Police said the operation was to serve a warrant on one of the militants, and the militant and his comrades resisted arrest, resulting in an armed encounter.
